t.p: glassmaking confined to Murano from 1291; peak 15th–16th c.; revivals after 1866 and in the 1920s
t.d: Venetian hot-worked soda glass, including chandeliers of hand-shaped flowers and leaves.
t.tech: hot-working, filigrana, murrine, sommerso, gilding and enamel
t.auth: 'Artistic Glass Murano' trademark (1994) certifies Murano manufacture; Asian and Eastern European imitations are common.

t.r: Byzantium, Russia and the Orthodox world
t.d: Devotional panel painting of the Orthodox Church; icons themselves sit in F4 as devotional panel paintings.
t.tech: painting on panel in a fixed iconographic canon
t.auth: Rublev's Trinity (c. 1410) is the only work fully authenticated as his; most icons are unsigned.

t.d: Tibetan Buddhist painted or textile scroll images for teaching and meditation; thangkas themselves sit in F4 as devotional scroll paintings.
t.tech: distemper (pigment in animal glue) on cotton; appliqué and embroidery
t.mat: cotton, silk, mineral and organic pigments, gold
t.auth: Rarely signed; old pieces often have a mantra or inscription on the back; poster reproductions are common.

t.d: Movement begun with Harvey Littleton's 1962 Toledo workshops, making glass in artists' studios.
t.tech: glassblowing, flameworking, casting, kiln-forming, cold working
t.auth: Signed and dated studio work

t.d: Art Nouveau group organised in 1901 under Émile Gallé; members included Daum, Majorelle and Vallin.
t.auth: Signatures with Cross of Lorraine

t.d: Miniature toggle carving for the cord of hanging pouches, a sculptural art in its own right.
t.auth: carver's signature (common from the 18th century), wear around cord holes; later copies and resin casts exist

t.d: Carving of New Zealand pounamu into taonga such as hei-tiki, hei matau and pekapeka.
t.tech: abrasive rubbing, shaping with sticks and water, long polishing
t.auth: Pounamu is found only in New Zealand; much souvenir 'greenstone' is imported jade.

t.d: Lost-wax brass heads, plaques and figures made by a royal guild for the oba's palace and ancestral altars.

t.d: Naturalistic small bronzes of animals and hunting scenes, issued in editions for middle-class interiors.
t.tech: sand and lost-wax casting, mechanical reduction, patination
t.auth: cast-through signature and foundry seal; lifetime casts are crisper than later ones from worn moulds

t.d: Tiny-tessera glass mosaics from the Vatican Mosaic Studio, sold on the Grand Tour.

t.p: Northern Song (960–1127) onward; leading style from the Yuan

t.tech: brush and ink, minimal colour, with poetry and calligraphy
t.auth: Forgery is common: Zhang Daqian (1899–1983) made fakes bought by nearly every major US art museum; check seals, colophons, paper and provenance.

t.d: Miniature painting of the Deccan sultanates.

t.d: Temple-market watercolours by Patua painters.
t.auth: Antique paper and pigments; later revivals common.

t.d: Hereditary workshop of professional painters serving the shogunates, from Kanō Masanobu (1434–1530).
t.tech: ink painting and colour-and-gold on paper
t.auth: Many screens are school works; a named master needs strong provenance.

t.d: Saint retablos and narrative ex-votos on tin.
t.tech: oil on tin with written testimony
ctr: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
t.auth: Dated inscription, aged tin; modern works often on paper.

t.d: Korean folk painting by mostly anonymous itinerant painters, with lucky and protective meanings.
t.auth: Modern revival works and decorative reproductions are common.

t.d: Women's wall and floor painting moved onto paper and canvas.
t.tech: Bharni, Kachni, Tantrik, Godna, Kohbar styles
t.auth: GI-registered; natural pigments and named artist.

t.d: Court painting of the Mughal emperors, fusing Persian and Indian traditions.
t.auth: Later provincial and Company-style works and copies are common; reign style helps dating.

t.d: Japanese-style painting in mineral pigments and nikawa glue on washi or silk, named to distinguish it from yōga.
t.tech: brush painting with layered mineral pigments, gold or silver leaf
t.mat: washi, silk, mineral pigments, nikawa glue, gofun
t.auth: Pigment layering and ground; modern copies are common.

t.d: Hill-state miniature painting, chiefly Basohli, Guler and Kangra.
t.tech: fine line, cool colour, naturalistic landscape
t.auth: Kangra became a name for the whole school; attribution by family workshop.

t.d: Cloth and palm-leaf painting for Jagannath worship and sung scrolls.
t.tech: gum-chalk primed cloth, Mota Kala and Saru Kala lines
t.mat: cotton cloth, palm leaf, mineral pigments
t.auth: GI registered 2008 (Odisha) and 2018 (Bengal).

t.d: Small paintings on paper for manuscripts and albums.
t.tech: fine brushwork in opaque colour, gold
t.auth: Leaves from dispersed manuscripts circulate; check text, borders and provenance; later and modern work continues the style.

t.d: Rajput court painting of Rajasthan, classified by Coomaraswamy in 1916.
t.auth: School style and court inscriptions guide attribution.

t.d: Decorative painting style of plants and gods on gold or silver ground, founded by Kōetsu and Sōtatsu.
t.tech: bold flat design, gold and silver ground
t.mat: mineral colours, ink, gold and silver leaf on paper
t.auth: Not a hereditary school; later copies and followers' works are common.

t.d: Popular painting under glass, from religious images to scenes of daily life.
t.auth: Signed works by named painters are sought after.

t.d: Vietnamese fine-art lacquer painting developed at the École Supérieure des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine in Hanoi.
t.tech: layered lacquer, sanded and polished; eggshell for white; silver leaf
t.mat: sơn tree lacquer, eggshell, seashell, silver leaf, board
t.auth: A work can take months of layering; check layer depth and signature.

t.d: Enamel painting of animals and scenes for the tourist market.
t.auth: Signature; cooperative provenance.

t.d: White geometric figures on ochre or mud walls.
t.auth: GI registered.

t.d: Acrylic painting of Dreaming stories begun at Papunya.
t.auth: Buy through art centres or Indigenous Art Code signatories; works over A$250 should carry a certificate on art-centre or gallery letterhead matching the work; a photo of the artist is not a certificate.

t.r: China (Tianjin, Shandong, Suzhou, Hebei, Shaanxi, Sichuan)
t.p: Tang origins; flourished late Ming to Qing; revived as heritage industry
t.d: Coloured woodblock pictures printed for decoration and ritual at Chinese New Year.
t.tech: design pasted on a board and carved in relief; one block per colour, sometimes hand-coloured
t.auth: few authentic examples date before the 19th century; most on the market are later or revival printings

t.d: Commercial colour woodblock prints of actors, beauties and famous places, produced by a publisher with designer, carver and printer.

t.auth: censor seals (kiwame and others, 1790–1876) and publisher seals date a print; early impressions have crisp lines and intended colours, late ones worn blocks and changed colours; 20th-century re-carved reproductions exist
